root_cause.text: In KVM’s nested SVM LBR virtualization, `svm_copy_lbrs()` incorrectly unconditionally marked the destination VMCB’s `VMCB_LBR` clean bit dirty, so when `nested_svm_vmexit()` used it on `vmcb12` it illegally cleared a clean bit in the nested guest-controlled VMCB.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR)` from `svm_copy_lbrs()` and notes that `nested_svm_vmexit()` copies LBRs to `vmcb12`, where “clearing clean bits in vmcb12 is not architecturally defined”; it also moves `vmcb_mark_dirty()` to callers and skips it for `vmcb12`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark VMCB02 LBR state dirty after preparing nested save data so updated LBR state is correctly tracked.
intent_record.what: A new call to `vmcb_mark_dirty(vmcb02, VMCB_LBR);` was inserted immediately after the LBR save/copy logic in `nested_vmcb02_prepare_save()`, before the existing `svm_update_lbrv(&svm->vcpu);` call.
intent_record.how: This ensures the VMCB02 LBR state is marked dirty after it is prepared, so the updated last-branch-record state will be recognized as modified and properly propagated or saved during nested virtualization handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark the VMCB LBR state dirty after copying it in the non-LBRV path to ensure nested LBR state is properly propagated.
intent_record.what: The conditional around the LBR copy was expanded to use braces, and a new call to vmcb_mark_dirty(vmcb01, VMCB_LBR) was added in the else branch after svm_copy_lbrs(vmcb01, vmcb02).
intent_record.how: When LBR virtualization is not enabled for the nested guest, the code still copies LBR state from vmcb01 to vmcb02 and now explicitly marks the VMCB LBR state as dirty so the update will be recognized and propagated correctly. This prevents the copied LBR state from being treated as clean and potentially lost or ignored.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop redundantly marking the LBR VMCB state dirty after copying it.
intent_record.what: The call to vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR) was removed from svm_copy_lbrs(), leaving only the assignments that copy the LBR-related save fields from the source VMCB to the destination VMCB.
intent_record.how: The function still copies the LBR state values, but it no longer explicitly marks the LBR portion of the destination VMCB as dirty after the copy. This changes bookkeeping for VMCB updates and may affect whether the hypervisor treats the copied LBR state as needing to be written back or synchronized.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally marks the destination VMCB's LBR area dirty after copying, which is the direct cause of illegally clearing/overwriting the nested guest-controlled clean bit when the destination is vmcb12.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally marks the destination VMCB's LBR state dirty after copying, which is the root cause of the bug: when the destination is vmcb12 in nested SVM exit handling, it clears a clean bit in guest-controlled state.

commit 1d5a1b5860ed6f623071329112e5935db043eb55
Author: Maxim Levitsky <mlevitsk@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Mar 22 19:40:45 2022 +0200

    KVM: x86: nSVM: correctly virtualize LBR msrs when L2 is running
    
    When L2 is running without LBR virtualization, we should ensure
    that L1's LBR msrs continue to update as usual.
    
    Signed-off-by: Maxim Levitsky <mlevitsk@redhat.com>
    Message-Id: <20220322174050.241850-2-mlevitsk@redhat.com>
    Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is an unconditional dirtying of the destination VMCB's LBR clean bit inside `svm_copy_lbrs()`. In this commit, the function body still contains `vmcb_mark_dirty(to_vmcb, VMCB_LBR);`, but the surrounding usage shows the fix is already present for the nested case: `svm_enable_lbrv()` calls `svm_copy_lbrs(svm->vmcb, svm->vmcb01.ptr);` and `svm_disable_lbrv()` calls `svm_copy_lbrs(svm->vmcb01.ptr, svm->vmcb);`, i.e. the code now explicitly moves the LBR MSRs between vmcb01 and vmcb02 depending on state. More importantly, the commit adds `svm_update_lbrv()` and `svm_get_lbr_msr()` to choose the correct VMCB based on `LBR_CTL_ENABLE_MASK`, and `svm_set_msr()` now writes `dbgctl` either to `svm->vmcb` or `svm->vmcb01.ptr` followed by `svm_update_lbrv(vcpu)`. So while the dirty-mark call is still present, this snippet shows the commit's corrected handling is already in place and the previously vulnerable behavior is not present as an active bug in this version.
